_meta.scope: Greenfield (city, county seat), Fortville (town) and McCordsville (town), all in Hancock County
_meta.fair_housing: Places, rules, services and infrastructure only. No demographic, school, crime or 'family' content was collected. The McCordsville 2040 Comprehensive Plan has household-composition, age, race and income tables and describes the school district as a draw; none of that was used. Only unit counts, subdivision names, utility providers, road names and the McCord Square plan were taken from it. Fortville's rental ordinance defines 'family' for occupancy purposes. That definition was left out, along with its occupancy and group-home clauses. The Fortville and Greenfield town sites link to the local school corporation, and those links were ignored. The Greenfield comprehensive plan has a population projection, and only its housing-unit projection was used.
_meta.note: Every URL in 'sources' was opened during this pass. Municipal codes were searched in full text through American Legal's search API (codelibrary.amlegal.com/api/search, scoped to each client: greenfieldin, fortvillein, mccordsville) for 'rental', 'landlord', 'rental unit', 'rental property', 'rental registration', 'short-term rental', 'short term rental', 'vacation rental', 'tourist home', 'bed and breakfast' and 'property maintenance'. None of the three codes is fully current, so newer council action was checked separately. Fortville's code runs through Jan 2023, Greenfield's through Dec 2024 and McCordsville's through Feb 2025. Greenfield's UDO PDF (and its proposed 2027 rewrite) and Fortville's zoning ordinance PDF were text-searched in full; McCordsville's zoning (Ch. 154) is inside its American Legal code. Distances are straight-line from Monument Circle, computed from Wikipedia's town coordinates: McCordsville 14.9 mi, Fortville 20.1 mi, Greenfield 21.4 mi.
_meta.state_law: See owner-facts-west-south.json _meta for IC 36-1-20 (rental registration: $5/yr fee cap, inspection limits for professionally managed units), IC 36-1-24 (STRs) and IC 6-1.1-20.6-7.5 (2% cap). Fortville's 2026 ordinance cites IC 36-1-20 as its authority.
_meta.county_court: Hancock County local rule LR30-AR00-2 (caseload allocation plan, as amended effective January 8, 2025) dockets EV (eviction) cases in the Hancock Circuit Court and Superior Court No. 1. Civil cases in those two courts are assigned at random by the Clerk. SC (small claims) goes to Superior Court No. 2. The county's Superior Court I page lists evictions among its case types, and its Superior Court II page lists small claims. All three courts sit in the Hancock County Courthouse, 9 E. Main St., Greenfield (Circuit Rm 302, Superior I Rm 303, Superior II Rm 217).

greenfield.jurisdiction: City of Greenfield, county seat of Hancock County (chosen April 1828) and the county's largest municipality, per its comprehensive plan. It lies in Center and Brandywine townships (Wikipedia).
greenfield.rental_rules: None found. The Greenfield Code of Ordinances (2025 S-4, local legislation current through Ord. 2024-44, passed 12-11-2024) has no rental registration, licensing, or inspection chapter. Searches for 'rental unit', 'rental registration' and 'landlord' (outside the fair-housing chapter) return nothing. A landlord registration ordinance ($5 one-time fee) failed 4-2 on second reading on September 11, 2024, per the Daily Reporter. The one rental-specific code rule is Sec. 91.136: in rental dwelling units the owner, manager, or rental agent must install the required smoke detectors and repair or replace one within seven business days of written notice.
greenfield.short_term_rentals: No Greenfield short-term rental rule found. The UDO (DocumentCenter/View/482, revised 13 November 2024) and the proposed 2027 UDO (Ord. 2026-28 exhibits) only define a 'Short-Term Lodging Agreement' (rooms for a fee for less than 30 days) and regulate bed-and-breakfasts as an operator-occupied conditional use. They have no STR use or permit, so state law (IC 36-1-24) governs.
greenfield.eviction_court: Eviction (EV) cases are docketed in the Hancock Circuit Court and Hancock Superior Court No. 1, assigned at random by the Clerk (local rule LR30-AR00-2, effective January 8, 2025). Small claims go to Superior Court No. 2. All three courts are in the Hancock County Courthouse, 9 E. Main St., Greenfield.
greenfield.property_tax: Billed by the Hancock County Treasurer (111 American Legion Place, Suite 205, Greenfield); 2026 installments due May 11 and November 10. A non-homestead single-family rental is capped at 2% of gross assessed value, before voter-approved referendum levies.

utilities.water: City of Greenfield Water Utility. Residential water deposit is $50; renters must provide a copy of their lease when starting service.
utilities.sewer: City of Greenfield Wastewater Utility; the city also runs a stormwater utility.
utilities.electric: Greenfield Power and Light (GP&L), the city-owned electric utility, serving customers within city limits. Residential electric deposit is $100 with gas heat or $150 all-electric. The comprehensive plan notes the city owns its electric utility.
utilities.gas: The city's utility list names 'Vectren' (now CenterPoint Energy). The page is dated.

greenfield.location: About 21 miles east of downtown Indianapolis (straight line). US 40 runs through downtown as Main Street, SR 9 (State Street) crosses it downtown, and I-70 runs along the city's north side. The comprehensive plan notes a new I-70 interchange under construction at CR 200W. Landmarks from the city's plan include the Pennsy Trail through downtown, the James Whitcomb Riley home on Main Street, Riley Park (with Brandywine Creek and a splash pad), and the Depot Street area downtown.
greenfield.new_construction: The city adopted its 'Greenfield In Gear' comprehensive plan (Roadmap to 2055) on June 11, 2025 (Resolution 2025/07). It projects a need for 7,778 more housing units by 2055 (from 9,488 in 2020 to 17,266). A UDO rewrite (Ord. 2026-28, '2027' UDO) responds to 2026 Public Law 73: it permits triplexes and quadplexes by right in the RM, RU, DT and TN districts, adds an ADU definition, and drops some design rules. The staff memo says developers of two existing projects asked to switch two-family lots to single-family because paired villas weren't selling. No city building-permit count was found.
unverified: Whether Greenfield revived a rental registration proposal in 2025-2026. The code is current only through Dec 2024, and the only coverage found is the failed September 2024 vote. Search results for a 2026 'Greenfield rental registry' are Greenfield, Massachusetts (recorder.com), not Indiana.
Adoption status of the 2027 UDO (Ord. 2026-28): the memo describes Plan Commission hearings in September and October 2026 and the ordinance going to Council, but final passage was not confirmed.
Gas: the city page still says 'Vectren'; confirm CenterPoint service territory.
Trash: no city page describing residential trash service was found (only heavy-item and leaf pickup pages).
Township list (Center and Brandywine) and the I-70 exit numbers rest on Wikipedia.

Treasurer page does not say when bills are mailed.

fortville.jurisdiction: Town of Fortville, in Vernon Township, northern Hancock County. Platted in 1849 and incorporated in 1865, per the town's history page.
fortville.rental_rules: Registration required. Ordinance 2026-8A, adopted August 17, 2026, adds Chapter 157 (Rental Housing Registration and Inspection) to the town code. It is not yet in the American Legal code, which runs only through Jan 2023. The town's registration form (dated 9.1.2026) requires a separate form per property and a $5 registration fee, waived 9-1-26 to 12-31-26. The owner must certify that no homestead deduction is claimed on the rental. A new owner must report the change and pay $5 within 30 days. The owner must keep an up-to-date tenant contact list. An owner who doesn't live in Hancock County or within 50 miles of town must name a local agent. Per the ordinance text in the second-reading council packet, inspections are complaint-driven, not routine. There is no fee if no violation is found; an uncured violation after 30 days costs $250, and re-inspections are $250 then $500. Exemptions cover owner-occupied single-family homes and 5+ unit 'rental unit communities' managed by a licensed real estate manager, so a managed single-family rental is not exempt. Separately, the utility code (Res. 2013-2A) keeps sewer and stormwater charges with the property owner until ownership legally transfers. On a rental, an unpaid sewer bill brings a notice to the owner and, 60 days later, a lien. The town may require the owner, not the tenant, to open service on a rental.
fortville.short_term_rentals: No Fortville short-term rental rule found. Neither the town code nor the Zoning Ordinance (adopted Ord. 2020-1C, amended through Ord. 2022-12C, 1-3-2023) defines or regulates STRs. The zoning ordinance treats a bed-and-breakfast facility as an owner-occupied use by special exception. State law (IC 36-1-24) governs.
fortville.eviction_court: Eviction (EV) cases are docketed in the Hancock Circuit Court and Hancock Superior Court No. 1, assigned at random by the Clerk (local rule LR30-AR00-2, effective January 8, 2025). Small claims go to Superior Court No. 2. All three courts are in the Hancock County Courthouse, 9 E. Main St., Greenfield.
fortville.property_tax: Billed by the Hancock County Treasurer (111 American Legion Place, Suite 205, Greenfield); 2026 installments due May 11 and November 10. A non-homestead single-family rental is capped at 2% of gross assessed value, before voter-approved referendum levies. Fortville's rental registration also requires certifying that no homestead deduction is claimed.

utilities.water: Fortville Water Works, the town's own municipal water utility, which also serves areas outside town limits (including designated parts of McCordsville under a 2026 interlocal agreement). To start service a tenant needs the signed signature page of the lease, which must also bear the landlord's signature. The account must be in the renter's name, and a deposit is required (amount not stated). Meters are read on the 15th, bills go out on the 1st, and payment is due by the 17th.
utilities.sewer: Town wastewater and stormwater, on the same Fortville Water Works bill. Financial responsibility for sewer and stormwater stays with the owner until ownership legally transfers. Unpaid sewer on a non-owner-occupied property leads to an owner notice, then a lien no sooner than 60 days later (code 50.08).
utilities.trash: Town-contracted trash collection; the monthly fee is charged to owners of single-family and duplex properties served under the town contract (code 54.06).
utilities.electric: Not confirmed from an official source.
utilities.gas: Not confirmed from an official source.

fortville.location: About 20 miles northeast of downtown Indianapolis (straight line). Main Street carries US 36/SR 67, and Town Hall is at 714 E. Broadway. Downtown grew along Main Street after the Bee Line Railroad arrived in 1852. The town's 33-acre Memorial Park (established 1920) holds ball diamonds, courts, a skate park, a dog park and the community center. Landmark Park is slated to open in spring 2027, and the Carnegie library dates to 1918.
fortville.new_construction: The Planning & Building Department's 2025 year-end report shows 194 new single-family permits in 2025. That is up from 84 in 2024, 50 in 2023, 59 in 2022 and 113 in 2021 (99 in 2020, 72 in 2019, 69 in 2018, 58 in 2017). The 2025 permits by subdivision were Beyers Estates 99, Northwest Fortville 62 and Mt. Vernon North 33. Multi-family units were 86 in 2023, 42 in 2022 and none in 2025. The town's planning page posts the 2014 'Envision Fortville' comprehensive plan and a 10-year land-use plan (2034).
unverified: Final adopted text of Ord. 2026-8A: the ordinance details above (complaint-only inspections, $250/$500 fees, exemptions) come from the unnumbered draft in the August 17, 2026 second-reading packet. The town form confirms adoption that day but shows a fee waiver through 12-31-26, while the draft said fees were waived until 11-1-26 and existing units had to register between 8-1-26 and 11-1-26. So the adopted text changed at least on dates. Get the signed ordinance from the Clerk-Treasurer before stating deadlines.

Legal question for counsel: IC 36-1-20-4.1 bars local inspection of, or inspection fees on, a unit managed by a professional real estate manager that had a qualifying third-party inspection in the prior 12 months. Fortville's exemption is narrower (only 5+ unit communities). Whether state law shields Red Door-managed single-family homes from Fortville inspections/fees isn't settled here.

mccordsville.jurisdiction: Town of McCordsville (incorporated 1988), in Vernon Township in the northwest corner of Hancock County, bordering Lawrence (Marion County) and Fishers (Hamilton County), per the town's comprehensive plan.
mccordsville.rental_rules: None found. The McCordsville Code of Ordinances (2025 S-5, local legislation current through Ord. 121024B, passed 2-11-2025) has no rental registration, licensing, or inspection chapter, and 'landlord' appears only in the fair-housing chapter. The town's posted new-ordinance list (newest May 2024) has nothing on rental housing. One practical point: town sewer, stormwater and trash fees follow the deed, not the occupant. Per the utility FAQ, the deed holder is responsible for the monthly fees even if they don't live there, and unpaid fees can become a lien. An owner renting out a home fills out Section 2 of the customer form alongside the tenant.
mccordsville.short_term_rentals: No McCordsville short-term rental rule found. The zoning ordinance (Ch. 154) has no STR use or definition. It defines and lists a bed-and-breakfast establishment (including tourist homes) as a separate use, mostly by special exception. State law (IC 36-1-24) governs.
mccordsville.eviction_court: Eviction (EV) cases are docketed in the Hancock Circuit Court and Hancock Superior Court No. 1, assigned at random by the Clerk (local rule LR30-AR00-2, effective January 8, 2025). Small claims go to Superior Court No. 2. All three courts are in the Hancock County Courthouse, 9 E. Main St., Greenfield.
mccordsville.property_tax: Billed by the Hancock County Treasurer (111 American Legion Place, Suite 205, Greenfield); 2026 installments due May 11 and November 10. A non-homestead single-family rental is capped at 2% of gross assessed value, before voter-approved referendum levies.

utilities.water: Citizens Energy Group, billed directly by Citizens; McCordsville has no municipal water utility. A 2026 interlocal agreement lets Fortville Water Works serve designated areas of McCordsville as they develop.
utilities.sewer: Town of McCordsville wastewater (treatment plant capacity 1.0 million gallons per day) for most of town. The part of town south of CR 650N is served by Aqua Indiana, a private utility, and the town notes about 500 septic systems remain. The town's utility office bills wastewater, stormwater and trash together. Fees follow the deed, sewer cannot be shut off, and unpaid balances can become a lien.
utilities.trash: Priority Waste under a town contract (January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2032), $18.48 a month on the town utility bill, with weekly trash and biweekly recycling.
utilities.electric: NineStar Connect (a Hancock County cooperative) or AES Indiana, depending on location, per the comprehensive plan.
utilities.gas: CenterPoint Energy, per the comprehensive plan.

mccordsville.location: About 15 miles northeast of downtown Indianapolis (straight line; the town's plan says less than 20 miles). US 36/SR 67 runs through town as W Broadway, SR 234 begins there, and Mt. Comfort Road (CR 600W) is the main north-south road. A CSX freight line crosses town at grade at Broadway; a 2021 cost estimate for an underpass there came to about $78 million. McCord Square, the town center, is a public-private development at the southeast corner of W Broadway and Mt. Comfort Road. Phase I (48 acres) includes IU Health, NineStar Connect offices and the police headquarters, and the town expects about 130 acres at build-out. Town parks include Old School Park and Town Hall Park.
mccordsville.new_construction: Per the McCordsville 2040 Comprehensive Plan (Plan Commission recommendation 7-0 on May 20, 2025; the town's planning page says it is adopted): more than three-quarters of the town's housing has been built since 2000, and about 9,500 residential units are existing or approved. In Q1 2025, 13 active residential projects were approved to pull building permits and 7 more had zoning approval but no permits yet. The largest neighborhoods once complete will be McCord Square (670), Jacobi Farms (650), Villages at Brookside (579) and Gateway Crossing (565). McCord Square is expected to hold 1,000 to 1,800 residential units at build-out. The plan counts 1,315 traditional rental apartment units. From the town's 2021 Annual Report: 437 new single-family permits in 2021, up from 240 in 2020, after 88-147 a year from 2013 to 2019.
unverified: Single-family permit counts after 2021: no 2022-2025 McCordsville annual report or permit summary was found on the town's sites (the development dashboard is a map with no totals).

Town Council adoption date of the 2040 Comprehensive Plan: the plan only carries the Plan Commission's May 20, 2025 certification; the town says it 'has adopted' the plan but the council ordinance date wasn't seen.

Rental registration after Feb 2025: the code is current only through Ord. 121024B (2-11-2025) and the town's new-ordinance list stops at May 2024. Council agendas from 2025-2026 were not reviewed one by one, so a later rental ordinance can't be fully ruled out (none surfaced in searches).
The Fortville water interlocal agreement was in Fortville's August 17, 2026 packet for consideration; whether both councils approved it, and which areas are designated, was not confirmed.
Electric and gas providers come from the town's comprehensive plan, not from the utilities' own territory maps.
Incorporation year (1988) and Vernon Township rest on Wikipedia.
